summary: The new boundary is the missing pray.c doturn() extended command. At step 643 the assigned recording, after #enhance completes, enters #turn as a lawful Knight: the role gate passes, gnostic conduct increments, halu_gname() resolves Lugh, can_chant() succeeds, the hero is not an evil or undead form, anger is within the allowed limit, and the hero is not in Gehennom. JavaScript has the extcmdlist row but no doturn handler, so dispatch falls through to its unported extended-command refusal. Port doturn() together with its pray.c maybe_turn_mon_iter() callback and wire the doturn dispatch; this is source-general pray.c file-port scope.

source.branch: For a Cleric or Knight with a chantable current form, doturn() records gnostic conduct and resolves the deity name. The normal branch requires a non-hostile hero form/alignment, ugangr <= 6, and !Inhell; it exercises Wisdom, computes the squared turning radius, iterates monsters, then calls nomul(-(5 - ((ulevel - 1) / 6))) and stores the multi reason and wake message before returning ECMD_TIME. Other source branches cover non-Cleric/Knight spell fallback or refusal, strangulation/speech failure, hostile demon-or-undead form or angry god, and Gehennom. maybe_turn_mon_iter() only acts on monsters within couldsee() and the radius that are nonpeaceful and undead, vampire-shifters, or high-level demons; confusion clears flee/paralysis, resistance and monster class thresholds choose peaceful conversion, death, or monflee().
